title: API key backfill mismatch after auth-conductor migration causes intermittent org ownership flip
creator: Asha Patel
description: Several Dedicated and Private customers reported intermittent authorization flips where API requests briefly appeared to be scoped to the wrong organization after a backfill run that followed the migration of the auth-conductor service. Symptoms included cross-org read access for metadata-only endpoints and transient 403s for the rightful org. This ticket tracks investigation, customer mitigation, the code fix, and rollout plan.
impact_summary: 3 Tier-1 Dedicated customers and 2 Private installations experienced transient authorization mis-scoping for metadata endpoints (org.list, model.catalog.metadata) over a ~6 hour window immediately after an automated backfill job. No data exfiltration of model artifacts or user content detected; scoped to lightweight metadata. Customer support escalations and potential compliance risk for Private deployments.
steps_to_reproduce: Run the legacy->new auth-conductor migration in a staging cluster that also executes the api-key org-backfill job
Trigger a concurrent API key lookup using the old fast-path cache (simulated by an edge proxy with cached entries)
Observe intermittent org_id returned by /internal/auth/resolve when cache hits collide with in-progress backfill writes
Replay with race window increased by running multiple backfill workers and a simulated high read QPS to the auth-resolver
customer_reports: CUST-REDWOOD-145: Dedicated customer reported read access to partner org model metadata during morning traffic spike
CUST-SEC-22: Private deployment audit flagged transient 403s affecting scheduled jobs during backfill window
root_cause: A timing window between the new auth-conductor's backfill process (which writes canonical org bindings) and the read-path fast-path cache invalidation. The migration changed the backfill to perform batched writes and emit a 'backfill-complete' signal in a separate control partition. Edge caches still used a stale validation epoch; during the batched-write window, interleaved reads could sample a partially-updated mapping and then be cached, causing incorrect org scoping for subsequent requests.
mitigation_actions: Rollback: Temporarily pause automated backfills in affected clusters (done 2026-03-13 09:40 UTC)
Hotfix: Introduce a per-key backfill marker and short TTL (30s) that marks keys as 'in-flight' so reads will bypass fast-path cache during backfill (PR deployed to staging)
Customer communication: Notified affected customers and provided audit logs and timeline (conversations linked below)
Monitoring: Added a temporary alert that detects >0.1% org-mismatch errors on metadata endpoints
fix_summary: Implement atomic backfill write with immediate cache invalidation and transition to optimistic compare-and-swap (CAS) per API key. Additionally, make the backfill emit synchronous in-memory signaling to the auth-resolver so it can avoid caching keys until the write completes.
customer_followups: Provide full audit export covering 2026-03-13 03:00-12:00 UTC for affected customers
Arrange technical callback with Dedicated account engineers to review fix and validate Private deployment patch
Offer extended log retention and compliance attestation for Private customers on request
qa_and_test_plan: Add fuzzed race tests that interleave backfill batched writes with parallel reads under high QPS
Add unit tests for CAS path and in-flight marker behavior
Run the backfill job in a canary environment with edge-proxy caching enabled for 48 hours before re-enabling in production
deployment_plan: Stage rollout to non-prod -> run canary backfill against staging edge cache (48h)
Deploy hotfix to one Dedicated region (eu-west-1) and monitor org-mismatch metric for 4h
Gradual 10/30/60/100% rollout to remaining regions with rollback window and pre-signed migration pause
Re-enable backfill automation only after two consecutive 24h windows with zero further mismatches
notes: Discussed trade-off: adding synchronous signaling increases coupling between backfill worker and auth-resolver but is low-risk vs. customers seeing org mismatch
Long-term: plan to move to event-sourced auth bindings that will avoid batched side-effect windows; tracked in project 'Auth Hardening Q2'
Edge-case: Private on-prem installs with air-gapped control plane require manual patching; SE team draft for 2026-03-15 is attached
